verdict.rationale: Kick documents period locking: once an accountant closes a period they lock it, the finalized books are protected from change by anyone, and reports for locked periods stay stable. Only non-financial actions like notes and receipts remain allowed. However, the evidence never documents an explicit unlock or reopening workflow, or who is permitted to perform it, so the 'without an explicit reopening' part of the story is only implied. Missing for 10: documented unlock/reopen workflow and permissions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an accountant, I can lock closed periods so prior-period numbers cannot change without an explicit reopening

citations.quote: When your accountant finishes reviewing and closing a period, they lock it. A lock protects the finalized books for that period from being changed - by anyone, including you.
Reports for locked periods remain accurate and stable.
Once a period is locked, you can still: View all transactions and reports for that period, Upload and attach receipts, Add notes to transactions
